locator.text: Display 160.6, p. 160, in the proof of Lemma C.1

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same inequality at every loop angle, with P_c(t) = p₁ + p₂ t and J_c(t) = p₂ - p₁ t exactly as on p. 159 and t = C/A the realized tilt. Two encoding points. (i) The paper names 𝒰 as 'the smaller root in v of 2(P_c-v)^2 = (v-2)J_c^2'; Lean writes that root in closed form, coneBound P J = P + J^2/4 - |J|√((P-2)/2 + J^2/16). These agree: the quadratic is 2v^2 - (4P+J^2)v + 2P^2 + 2J^2 = 0 (ConeAlgebra.boundary_polynomial), whose roots are P + J^2/4 ± |J|√((P-2)/2 + J^2/16), the minus sign being the smaller one; true_cone_iff and square_difference are the file's own link between the radical and the quadratic test. (ii) The Lean statement comes bundled: InTrueCone conjoins 2 < v < 𝒰 with 0 < a_L and 2 < P_c(t), so each declaration asserts the block's content and two further inequalities. No weakening in either direction was found.
